column2: “勿以太平而忘武备”。清顺治时一座射殿出现在奉先殿前，弓马骑射成为清代武备的核心。康熙帝曾亲率诸皇子和善射侍卫于此射箭，雍正时改为箭亭，乾隆帝在此召见殿试弓马成绩最优秀的武进士，嘉庆时箭亭亦被开辟为弓刀石的考试场地。

column4: "Do not forget military readiness in time of peace." Under the Shunzhi Emperor an archery hall stood before the Hall of Ancestral Worship, and mounted archery became the core of Qing military training. The Kangxi Emperor personally led the princes and skilled guards in archery here; under Yongzheng it was renamed the Arrow Pavilion; the Qianlong Emperor received here the military graduates who had excelled in the palace examination in riding and archery; and by the Jiaqing reign the pavilion also served as the examination ground for bow, sabre and stone-lifting.

column2: 故宫博物院收藏的清代宫廷珍宝，大部分出自紫禁城内掌管营造的造办处奉旨制作，还有一些是逢年节庆典时地方官吏的朝贡品。这些珍宝大都选用金、银、玉、翠、珍珠及各种宝石等名贵材质，征调各地著名匠师设计制造，竭尽巧思、不惜工本，一器之成往往经年累月，其工艺代表了当时的最高水平。

column4: Qing court treasures in the Palace Museum, most made to imperial order by the Imperial Household Workshops within the Forbidden City, with some presented as tribute by provincial officials at festivals and celebrations. Almost all use precious materials — gold, silver, jade, jadeite, pearls and assorted gemstones — and were designed and made by leading craftsmen summoned from across the empire, sparing neither ingenuity nor expense; a single object could take years to complete, and the workmanship represents the highest standard of its day.

column2: 故宫博物院收藏陶瓷类文物约 35 万件，绝大部分属原清宫旧藏，自成体系、流传有绪。本馆从中遴选 400 多件精品，按时代发展顺序展示，涵盖从红陶、灰陶、彩陶、黑陶、白陶到原始瓷、青瓷、黑瓷、白瓷以及颜色釉瓷和釉下彩、釉上彩瓷器，呈现中国陶瓷一万多年绵延不断的发展历程。陈列于武英殿正殿、工字廊与后殿敬思殿。

column4: The Palace Museum holds some 350,000 ceramic objects, the great majority from the former Qing court collection, forming a coherent body with a documented line of transmission. More than 400 of the finest are shown here in chronological order, covering red, grey, painted, black and white earthenware, proto-porcelain, celadon, black ware, white ware, monochrome glazes and underglaze- and overglaze-painted porcelain, presenting more than ten thousand years of continuous Chinese ceramic development. Displayed in the main hall of the Hall of Martial Valour, the I-shaped corridor and the rear Jingsi Hall.

column2: 故宫雕塑馆陈列在慈宁宫内，分雕塑荟萃馆、汉唐陶俑馆、砖石画像馆、修德白石馆、佛教造像馆五部分，陈列面积约 1375 平方米，展品总数 425 件。涵盖陶俑、画像砖石、佛像三大类：陶俑自战国至明代前后相续；陕北与晋西南画像石造型独特；河北曲阳白石佛像自北魏至隋唐纪年有序；宫廷旧藏中的永乐、宣德款藏传佛教铜造像体现明初宫廷风格，清代六世班禅像为清宫藏传佛教造像代表作。

column4: The Palace Museum's Sculpture Gallery, housed in the Palace of Compassion and Tranquillity, comprises five sections — sculpture highlights, Han and Tang pottery figures, pictorial bricks and stones, Quyang white marble, and Buddhist images — with about 1,375 square metres of display space and 425 objects. It covers three main categories: pottery figures running continuously from the Warring States to the Ming; the distinctive pictorial stones of northern Shaanxi and south-western Shanxi; the white marble Buddhas of Quyang, Hebei, securely dated from the Northern Wei through the Sui and Tang; and, from the former palace collection, Yongle- and Xuande-marked Tibetan Buddhist bronzes exemplifying early Ming court style, with the Qing image of the Sixth Panchen Lama representing Qing court Tibetan Buddhist sculpture.

Most are British, with others from France and Switzerland, and some made in Guangzhou, Suzhou and the palace clock workshop. Besides striking the hours and quarters, they use linked mechanisms to set figures, birds, beasts and flowers in continuous motion. The finest are selected for display here.
